what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Three API hosts follow the rule; all 296 live files match their manifests; the docs and the newsroom's own copies are where it did not reach.
sections.para: Every release a complete copy at its own path, never edited, with a manifest of hashes. Checked from outside on 22 November: 296 files, no mismatch. Two gaps: a version bump broke two explaining pages on api.send.sgit.ai, and 9 of the newsroom's copies have moved on from its last API release.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: The rule, three hosts, every file matching, a cheap copy, two gaps, and no release since 20 October.
sections.para: Seven points: the rule, the hosts, the check, the cost, the documentation gap, the newsroom's drift, and a month without a new release.

sections.label: The rule, as written
sections.line: A release is a directory at its own path, a complete copy, never edited, with every hash; a site pins one.
sections.para: The rule as api.send.sgit.ai wrote it on 20 October: whole copies instead of IFD's overlays, a manifest the gate recomputes, a live check after each deploy, and a one-line pin, or a copy into the site's own origin for pages that hold keys.

sections.label: Three hosts, six releases
sections.line: api.newsroom.sgit.ai has three releases, api.send.sgit.ai two, api.storyboards.sgit.ai one; the user and billing hosts are still proposals.
sections.para: What each host serves, its releases and sizes, and how storyboards differs: nested IFD-style paths and an integrity string per file.

sections.label: What we checked, and what held
sections.line: All 296 live files of six releases match their manifests; api.send.sgit.ai's v0.1.0 has not been edited, and v0.1.1 is a whole copy.
sections.para: How the check was done, its result (3,984,539 bytes, no mismatch), the git history of api.send.sgit.ai, and why 15 of its 36 files differ between releases.

sections.label: The first gap: the documentation is not under the rule
sections.line: A blanket version bump made api.send.sgit.ai's versioning and release pages say v0.1.1 starts as a copy of v0.1.1.
sections.para: The pages around a release are not under the rule; the commit that made v0.1.1 replaced the old version number in two passages, and the release checklist now copies a directory into itself.

sections.label: The second gap: the first site to move out has moved on
sections.line: The newsroom serves its own copies; 9 of the 74 files of api.newsroom.sgit.ai v0.2.5 were edited in the newsroom since, with no new release.
sections.para: 61 files identical, 4 changed by the move as the manifest lists, and 9 edited after the commit the release was cut from, between 15 October and 13 November.

sections.label: What a month says
sections.line: The rule held inside releases; the risk is at their edges. Two proposed checks would close the gaps.
sections.para: No host has cut a release since 20 October, so the fix-in-each-release and major-consolidation parts are untested. Proposed: put the explaining pages under the gate, and have the newsroom compare its copies with its pinned release.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Hashes prove bytes, not correctness; one day's check; the find-and-replace is a reading of a diff; our own interest.
sections.para: Five limits on what the check and the history show.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The api.send.sgit.ai pages, every manifest and file on three hosts, the Send API repository, and this repository, read on 22 November 2026.
